title: Accessibility and colimit closure of a compact filtered hull
statement: Use universes, accessibility, compactness, coherent functors and colimits from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe. Let $\mathcal E$ be a presentable infinity category, and let $\mathcal E_0\subseteq\mathcal E$ be an essentially small full subcategory that is replete (closed under equivalence), of $\kappa$-compact objects, closed under $\kappa$-small colimits computed in $\mathcal E$. Let $\mathcal E_1$ be the replete full subcategory consisting of objects equivalent to colimits of small $\kappa$-filtered diagrams taking values in $\mathcal E_0$. Then $\mathcal E_1$ is $\kappa$-accessible, admits all small colimits, and is closed under all small colimits computed in $\mathcal E$; its inclusion preserves these colimits. Every object of $\mathcal E_1$ has such a presentation indexed by the nerve of a small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered set. Every object of $\mathcal E_0$ belongs to $\mathcal E_1$.

source.place: Propositions 5.3.5.10 and 5.3.5.11(1) (fully faithful filtered extension); Proposition 5.4.2.2(3) (accessibility); Theorem 5.5.1.1(4) and Proposition 5.5.1.9 (all colimits and preservation); Proposition 5.3.1.18 (poset indexing). This is their compact-hull application in Lemma 5.5.4.14, printed p. 480.

proof.text: Essential smallness means there is a small $\mathcal C$ with an equivalence $q:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal E_0$. Fix its coherent inverse $r$. Compose $q$ with the full inclusion to obtain $i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$. For a $\kappa$-small diagram $a:K\to\mathcal C$, take the ambient colimit of $ia$. Its apex $z$ lies in $\mathcal E_0$ by closure; fullness makes the same cocone colimiting in $\mathcal E_0$: its mapping-space test is simply the ambient test restricted to targets in $\mathcal E_0$. Apply $r$ to this cocone. The inverse equivalences identify its mapping-space test with that for $a$, so it is colimiting in $\mathcal C$ and $i$ preserves it. Thus $\mathcal C$ admits all $\kappa$-small colimits and $i$ preserves them. Its image objects are $\kappa$-compact by hypothesis.

source.place: Setup of the application in Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480; equivalence and full-subcategory mapping-space argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability] to this small $\mathcal C$. The category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(\mathcal C)$ is $\kappa$-accessible and presentable, and every object has a small $\kappa$-filtered presentation by Yoneda objects. The functor $j:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ is fully faithful and preserves $\kappa$-small colimits.

Apply [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension] to $i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$. The target is presentable, so has small filtered colimits and is locally small. Step 1 checked full faithfulness, compactness and preservation of $\kappa$-small colimits. It gives a fully faithful extension $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E$ preserving all small colimits and satisfying $Fj\simeq i$. Its essential image is exactly $\mathcal E_1$: the forward inclusion follows by applying $F$ to the presentations of step 2; conversely a presentation $b:I\to\mathcal E_0$ lifts coherently to $rb:I\to\mathcal C$, and $F(\operatorname{colim}_I jrb)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I b$ by preservation and $qr\simeq1$. Repleteness supplies objects equivalent to these colimits.

source.place: Propositions 5.3.5.10-11 and 5.5.1.9; the essential-image identification is written out.

proof.text: By the equivalence-onto-essential-image clause of [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension] and step 3, $F$ factors as an equivalence $Q:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal E_1$ followed by its full inclusion $J$ into $\mathcal E$. For any small diagram $a:K\to\mathcal E_1$, use a coherent inverse of $Q$ to obtain $\widetilde a:K\to\mathcal A$. The cocone with apex $Q(\operatorname{colim}_K\widetilde a)$ is colimiting internally, because applying the inverse equivalence identifies its cocone universal property with the one in $\mathcal A$. Its image in $\mathcal E$ is the $F$-image of that colimit cocone, so is colimiting by step 3. Thus $\mathcal E_1$ admits all small colimits, is closed under ambient small colimits and $J$ preserves them, including the empty colimit. Local smallness follows by fullness. In particular its filtered colimits are ambient; the mapping spaces out of any $x\in\mathcal E_0$ are also ambient, so ambient $\kappa$-compactness gives internal $\kappa$-compactness. The essentially small $\mathcal E_0$ generates $\mathcal E_1$ under such colimits by definition. These are exactly the clauses of $\kappa$-accessibility.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.11(2); compact-hull argument of Lemma 5.5.4.14, p. 480, with explicit colimit tests.

proof.text: For a defining presentation $b:I\to\mathcal E_0$ of any $x\in\mathcal E_1$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-kappa-poset] to the small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory $I$. Its cofinal map $u:N(A)\to I$ has $A$ small and $\kappa$-filtered, and restriction of the ambient colimit cocone gives $x\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{N(A)}bu$, as required.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.18, p. 386; existing DAG node reused.

proof.text: For $x\in\mathcal E_0$, the one-object category $\Delta^0$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered index: every diagram into it has its unique extension to a cocone. The constant one-object diagram with value $x$ has colimit $x$, since its cocone test is the identity on each mapping space. Hence $x\in\mathcal E_1$. Closure under the empty colimit already follows from step 4; no empty filtered indexing category is used.
